sentences.text: Rapaxavi is an extinct enantiornithean bird belonging to the family Longipterygidae.
Its name translates to 'grasping bird,' highlighting a unique adaptation in its foot structure.
The type species for this genus is Rapaxavis pani.
The species name also references Pan, the Greek deity of forests, suggesting a tree-dwelling lifestyle.
A fossil initially assigned to Longirostravis was formally named Rapaxavis pani in 2009.
The specific epithet pani honors Pan Lijun, the individual who discovered the fossil.
The holotype, cataloged as DMNH D2522, is a nearly complete skeleton found in the Jiufotang Formation.
This specimen represents a subadult individual.
Initial preparation removed the right jugal bone, but later repairs at the Natural History Museum of Los Angeles County restored some damage.
A detailed redescription was published in 2011 following these restoration efforts.
Rapaxavis lived in Liaoning, China, during the Early Cretaceous Aptian stage, between 121.4 and 113.2 million years ago.
